title: Number — Duals, Sound Plurals & Personal Pronouns
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 5; Ryding Ch. 6 §§6.2–6.4)
objectives: Inflect dual nouns (-āni / -ayni) across nominative, accusative, and genitive cases.
Inflect sound masculine plurals (-ūna / -īna) and sound feminine plurals (-ātun / -ātin).
Use independent personal pronouns (هُوَ, هِيَ, أَنْتَ, أَنَا, etc.) as subjects of nominal sentences.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 4: Which short vowels mark nominative, accusative, and genitive on a regular singular noun?

sections.heading: Inflection by Letters (Al-Iʿrāb bi-l-Ḥurūf)
sections.body: Unlike singular nouns, which mark case with short vowels, duals and sound masculine plurals mark case through long-vowel letters. Both duals and sound plurals collapse the accusative and genitive into a single oblique ending.

sections.label: Dual & Sound Plural Endings
sections.summary: Dual: -āni (nom.) / -ayni (acc./gen.). Sound Masculine Plural (for male rational beings): -ūna (nom.) / -īna (acc./gen.). Sound Feminine Plural: -ātun (nom.) / -ātin (acc./gen.—never takes fatḥah!).

sections.heading: Dual & Sound Plural Declension
rows: Alif in rafʿ; yāʾ with fatḥah before it in naṣb/jarr
Wāw in rafʿ; yāʾ with kasrah before it in naṣb/jarr
Takes kasrah even in the accusative!

sections.translation: They are teachers in the school.
sections.irab: هُمْ: ضَمِيرٌ مُنْفَصِلٌ مَبْنِيٌّ فِي مَحَلِّ رَفْعٍ مُبْتَدَأٌ | مُعَلِّمُونَ: خَبَرٌ مَرْفُوعٌ بِالوَاوِ لِأَنَّهُ جَمْعُ مُذَكَّرٍ سَالِمٌ
sections.notes: Independent pronouns are invariable (mabnī) and stand as the definite mubtadaʾ. مُعَلِّمُونَ is nominative, marked by wāw.

sections.heading: Sound Feminine Plural Accusative
sections.body: A sound feminine plural (ending in ـَاتٌ) never takes fatḥah. Its accusative and genitive both end in kasrah: رَأَيْتُ المُعَلِّمَاتِ ('I saw the female teachers').
